facts: The paper 'Combinets: Creativity via Recombination of Neural Networks' (arXiv:1802.03605) was authored by Matthew Guzdial and Mark O. Riedl.

The research addresses the limitation that deep neural networks struggle with out-of-distribution inputs, especially when limited training data is available.
Existing transfer learning techniques typically require additional training (backpropagation) or domain-specific transfer mechanisms.
The authors introduce 'conceptual expansion', a general representation to reuse existing trained models to produce new models without backpropagation.
The approach is inspired by human creativity and the ability to make conceptual leaps from existing knowledge to create something surprising.
The method was evaluated on few-shot variations of two distinct tasks: image classification and image generation.
The proposed conceptual expansion approach outperforms standard transfer learning baselines on the evaluated few-shot tasks.
